QUESTION 11
Shall this Town of Reading accept sections 3 to 7, inclusive of chapter 44B of the General Laws, as approved by its legislative body, a summary of which appears below?
SUMMARY
Sections 3 to 7 of Chapter 44B of the General Laws of Massachusetts, also known as the Community Preservation Act, establish a dedicated funding source to enable cities and
towns to (1) acquire, create and preserve open space, which includes land for park and recreational uses and the protection of public drinking water well fields, aquifers and recharge
areas, wetlands, farm land, forests, marshes, beaches, scenic areas, wildlife preserves and other conversation areas, (2) rehabilitate and restore land for recreational use, (3) acquire,
preserve, rehabilitate and restore historic buildings and resources, (4) acquire, create, preserve and support affordable housing and (5) rehabilitate and restore open space and affordable
housing that was acquired or created with community preservation funds. If these sections are accepted, the funding sources for these community preservation purposes in the Town
of Reading under Section 3(b) of Chapter 44B will be (1) a surcharge of 1% on the annual property tax assessed on real property and (2) annual distributions made by the state from
a trust fund created by the Act. The surcharge will be assessed starting in fiscal year 2028, which begins on July 1, 2027.
The following will be exempt from the annual surcharge: (1) property owned and occupied as a domicile of a person who qualifies for low income housing, or low or moderate
income senior housing, as defined in the Act; (2) real property defined as commercial or industrial for property tax classification purposes under G.L. c. 59, § 2A in years a higher tax
rate is adopted for those properties; and (3) the real estate tax assessed on $100,000 of the value of each parcel of residential real property as defined for property tax classification
purposes. A taxpayer receiving a regular property tax abatement or exemption will also receive a pro rata reduction in the surcharge.
A Community Preservation Committee will be established by bylaw to study community preservation resources, possibilities and needs and to make annual recommendations
to Town Meeting on spending the funds. At least 10% of the revenues for each fiscal year will be spent or reserved for later spending on each of the Act’s community preservation
purposes: (1) open space including land for recreational uses, (2) historic resources and (3) affordable housing.
YES
NO

contests.title: North Reading — Question 10: Modular-classroom debt exclusion

provenance.quote:
Shall the Town of North Reading be allowed to exempt from the provisions of proposition two and one-half, so-called, the amounts required to pay for the bond issued in order to remove and replace the modular classrooms at the J. Turner Hood and E. Ethel Little Schools?
At October 2026 Town Meeting, North Reading voters appropriated $3,500,000.00 to remove and replace modular classrooms at Hood and Little Schools, to be bonded contingent on approval of Proposition 2 1/2 Debt Exclusion.
Proposition 2 ½ is a state law that caps the overall property tax “levy limit” on existing property to 2 ½ percent increases per year, plus tax revenue from new growth that adds to the town’s tax base. Question 10 proposes to temporarily increase property taxes above the amounts otherwise allowed under Proposition 2 ½. The increase is for the amount of the annual debt service payments for the approved project, and it lasts only for the life of the related borrowing.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows Reading to assess an additional $6.5 million in real estate and personal property taxes for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2027. The money would fund the general operation of public schools, police, fire, public works, the library and general government.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional $6.5 million in property taxes for these operations.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed additional property-tax authorization.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Adopts the Community Preservation Act funding system for Reading. A 1% surcharge on annual real-property taxes would begin in fiscal year 2028, starting July 1, 2027, supplemented by distributions from the state trust fund. The money could support open space and recreation, historic resources and affordable housing, including the acquisition, preservation and restoration work described in the question. Exemptions cover qualifying low-income homeowners and qualifying low- or moderate-income senior homeowners; commercial and industrial property in years when those properties have a higher tax rate; and the tax on the first $100,000 of each residential parcel’s value. Regular tax abatements or exemptions would proportionally reduce the surcharge. A Community Preservation Committee would recommend spending to Town Meeting. At least 10% of annual revenue would be spent or reserved for each of three purposes: open space, historic resources and affordable housing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve adopting this funding system, including its 1% real-property-tax surcharge, exemptions and spending rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject adopting this Community Preservation Act funding system through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Asks voters to express a nonbinding instruction to their state representative to support legislation or rules reducing the House Speaker’s and Senate President’s control over legislators’ stipends, or extra pay. It also asks that stipends go only to legislators doing significant extra work that is transparent and accountable to the public. This vote would not itself change the law or pay rules.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Express support for this nonbinding instruction about legislative stipends.
measureRecords.noMeans: Express opposition to this proposed nonbinding instruction.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Allows North Reading to collect property taxes above Proposition 2½ limits for annual payments on borrowing to remove and replace modular classrooms at the J. Turner Hood and E. Ethel Little schools. Town Meeting approved $3.5 million for the project, conditional on approval of this debt exclusion. The tax increase would last only for the life of the related borrowing.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve excluding this project’s annual debt payments from Proposition 2½ property-tax limits.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed debt exclusion for the classroom replacement project.
